name: Descent: major type
description: Major mode of descent (note: not in original EA; derived from variables describing patrilineal and matrilineal kin groups EA017, EA019 and EA021).

answers.name: Patrilineal
answers.description: Patrilineal (EA017 > 1, EA019 = 1, EA021 = 9)

answers.name: Duolateral
answers.description: Duolateral (EA017 > 1, EA019 > 1, EA021 = 9 or EA021 = 0)

answers.name: Matrilineal
answers.description: Matrilineal (EA017 = 1, EA019 > 1, EA021 = 9)

answers.name: Quasi-lineages
answers.description: Quasi-lineages (EA017 = 1, EA019 = 1, EA021 = 6)

answers.name: Ambilineal
answers.description: Ambilineal (EA017 = 1, EA019 = 1, EA021 = 3 or EA021 = 4 or EA021 = 5)

answers.name: Bilateral
answers.description: Bilateral (EA017 = 1, EA019 = 1, EA021 = 1 or EA021 = 2)

answers.name: Mixed
answers.description: Mixed (EA017  and/or EA019 > 1,and EA021 not equal to 9)

answers.name: Missing data
answers.description: Missing data

name: Kin terms for cousins
description: Extent to which names for cousins distinguish cousin subtypes and/or among other groups of kin.

answers.name: Crow
answers.description: Crow, i.e., FaSiCh equated with Fa or FaSi and/or MoBrCh with Ch or BrCh(ws)

answers.name: Descriptive
answers.description: Descriptive or derivative, rather than elementary, terms employed for all cousins

answers.name: Eskimo
answers.description: Eskimo, i.e., FaBrCh, FaSiCh, MoBrCh, and MoSiCh equated with each other but differentiated from siblings

answers.name: Hawaiian
answers.description: Hawaiian, i.e., all cousins equated with siblings or called by terms clearly derivative from those for siblings

answers.name: Iroquois
answers.description: Iroquois, i.e., FaSiCh equated with MoBrCh but differentiated from both siblings and parallel cousins

answers.name: Omaha
answers.description: Omaha, i.e., MoBrCh equated with MoBr or Mo and/or FaSiCh with SiCh(ms) or Ch

answers.name: Sudanese
answers.description: Sudanese, i.e., FaSiCh and MoBrCh distinguished alike from siblings, parallel cousins, and each other but without conforming to either the Crow, the descriptive, or the Omaha patterns

answers.name: Mixed
answers.description: Mixed or variant patterns not adequately represented by any of the foregoing symbols. The details are given under "Classification by Clusters."

answers.name: Missing data
answers.description: Missing data

name: Cousin marriages permitted
description: The rules or practices governing the marriageability or nonmarriageability of a man's first cousins and, in some cases, second cousins.

answers.name: Cross-cousin
answers.description: Duolateral cross-cousin marriage permitted, i.e., marriage allowed with either MoBrDa or FaSiDa but forbidden with a parallel cousin

answers.name: Paternal only
answers.description: Duolateral marriage permitted with paternal cousins only (FaBrDa or FaSiDa)

answers.name: Maternal only
answers.description: Duolateral marriage permitted with maternal cousins only (MoBrDa or MoSiDa)

answers.name: FaBrDa/MoBrDa only
answers.description: Duolateral marriage permitted with an uncle's daughter only (FaBrDa or MoBrDa)

answers.name: FaSiDa/MoSiDa only
answers.description: Duolateral marriage permitted with an aunt's daughter only (FaSiDa or MoSiDa)

answers.name: Matrilateral cross only
answers.description: Unilateral: only matrilateral cross-cousin marriage permitted, i.e., with a MoBrDa

answers.name: No first/second cousins
answers.description: Nonlateral marriage, i.e., unions forbidden with any first or second cousin

answers.name: No first cousins
answers.description: Nonlateral marriage, evidence available only for first cousins

answers.name: Patrilateral cross only
answers.description: Unilateral: only patrilateral cross-cousin marriage permitted i.e., with a FaSiDa

answers.name: Any first cousins
answers.description: Quadrilateral marriage, i.e., marriage allowed with any first cousin

answers.name: Some second only
answers.description: Nonlateral marriage in which all first cousins and some but not all second cousins are forbidden as spouses

answers.name: Only second cousins
answers.description: Nonlateral marriage in which unions are forbidden with any first cousin but are permitted with any second cousin (or at least any who is not a lineage mate)

answers.name: Trilateral
answers.description: Trilateral marriage, i.e., marriage allowed with any first cousin except an orthocousin or lineage mate

answers.name: Missing data
answers.description: Missing data

name: Marital composition: monogamy and polygamy
description: Marital composition of family units, regardless of whether families live as independent nuclear units or as part of larger extended families.

answers.name: Monogamous
answers.description: Monogamous

answers.name: Limited polygyny
answers.description: Polygynous, with polygyny occasional or limited

answers.name: Polygyny, sororal cohabit
answers.description: Polygynous, with polygyny common and preferentially sororal, and co-wives not reported to occupy separate quarters

answers.name: Polygyny, sororal separate quarters
answers.description: Polygynous, with polygyny common and preferentially sororal, and co-wives typically occupying separate quarters

answers.name: Polygyny, non-sororal separate quarters
answers.description: Polygynous, with polygyny general and not reported to be preferentially sororal, and co-wives typically occupying separate quarters

answers.name: Polygyny, non-sororal cohabit
answers.description: Polygynous, with polygyny general and not reported to be preferentially sororal, and co-wives not reported to occupy separate quarters

answers.name: Polyandrous
answers.description: Polyandrous

answers.name: Missing data
answers.description: Missing data

name: Marital residence with kin: prevailing pattern
description: The prevailing profile of marital residence in the society.

answers.name: Avunculocal
answers.description: Avunculocal, i.e., normal residence with or near the maternal uncle or other male matrilineal kinsmen of the husband

answers.name: Ambilocal
answers.description: Ambilocal, i.e., residence established optionally with or near the parents of either the husband or the wife, depending upon circumstances or personal choice, where neither alternative exceeds the other in actual frequency by a ratio greater than two to one.

answers.name: Avuncu-uxorilocal
answers.description: Optionally uxorilocal or avunculocal. This may be the case in a uxorilocal society where many men marry a MoBrDa and thus, in fact, live avunculocally

answers.name: Avuncu-virilocal
answers.description: Optionally patrilocal (or virilocal) or avunculocal

answers.name: Matrilocal
answers.description: Matrilocal, i.e., normal residence with or near the female matrilineal kinsmen of the wife. Cf. U Uxorilocal

answers.name: Neolocal
answers.description: Neolocal, i.e., normal residence apart from the relatives of both spouses or at a place not determined by the kin ties of either

answers.name: Separate
answers.description: Nonestablishment of a common household, i.e., where both spouses remain in their natal households, sometimes called "duolocal" or "natolocal" residence

answers.name: Patrilocal
answers.description: Patrilocal, i.e., normal residence with or near the male patrilineal kinsmen of the husband. Cf. V Virilocal

answers.name: Uxorilocal
answers.description: Uxorilocal. Equivalent to "matrilocal" but confined to instances where the wife's matrikin are not aggregated in matrilocal and matrilineal kin groups

answers.name: Virilocal
answers.description: Virilocal. Equivalent to "patrilocal" but confined to instances where the husband's patrikin are not aggregated in patrilocal and patrilineal kin groups

answers.name: Ambi-uxo
answers.description: Ambilocal, with a marked preponderance of uxorilocal practice (i.e., uxorilocal option exceeds virilocal option in actual frequency by a ratio greater than two to one).

answers.name: Ambi-viri
answers.description: Ambilocal, with a marked preponderance of virilocal practice (i.e., virilocal option exceeds uxorilocal option in actual frequency by a ratio greater than two to one).

answers.name: Missing data
answers.description: Missing data

name: Transactions at marriage: prevailing type
description: Prevailing type of transfer or exchange at marriage.

answers.name: Bride-wealth
answers.description: Bride-price or bride-wealth, i.e., transfer of a substantial consideration in the form of livestock, goods, or money from the groom or his relatives to the kinsmen of the bride

answers.name: Bride-service
answers.description: Bride-service, i.e., a substantial material consideration in which the principal element consists of labor or other services rendered by the groom to the bride's kinsmen

answers.name: Token bride-wealth
answers.description: Token bride-price, i.e., a small or symbolic payment only

answers.name: Gift exchange
answers.description: Gift exchange, i.e., reciprocal exchange of gifts of substantial value between the relatives of the bride and groom, or a continuing exchange of goods and services in approximately equal amounts between the groom or his kinsmen and the bride's relatives

answers.name: Woman exchange
answers.description: Exchange, i.e., transfer of a sister or other female relative of the groom in exchange for the bride

answers.name: Insignificant
answers.description: Absence of any significant consideration, or bridal gifts only

answers.name: Dowry
answers.description: Dowry, i.e., transfer of a substantial amount of property from the bride's relatives to the bride, the groom, or the kinsmen of the latter

answers.name: Missing data
answers.description: Missing data

name: Subsistence economy: dominant activity
description: Dominant mode of subsistence (note: not in original EA; derived from other variables on subsistence and type of agriculture).

answers.name: Gathering
answers.description: Gathering contributes most

answers.name: Fishing
answers.description: Fishing contributes most

answers.name: Hunting
answers.description: Hunting contributes most

answers.name: Pastoralism
answers.description: Pastoralism contributes most

answers.name: Casual agriculture
answers.description: Casual agriculture contributes most

answers.name: Extensive agriculture
answers.description: Extensive agriculture contributes most

answers.name: Intensive agriculture
answers.description: Intensive agriculture contributes most

answers.name: Two or more sources
answers.description: Two or more sources contribute equally

answers.name: Agriculture, type unknown
answers.description: Agriculture contributes most, type unknown

answers.name: Missing for at least 1 activity
answers.description: Missing data for at least one subsistence activity

answers.name: No agriculture
answers.description: Complete absence of agriculture

answers.name: Casual
answers.description: Casual agriculture, i.e., the slight or sporadic cultivation of food or other plants incidental to a primary dependence upon other subsistence practices

answers.name: Extensive/shifting
answers.description: Extensive or shifting cultivation, as where new fields are cleared annually, cultivated for a year or two, and then allowed to revert to forest or brush for a long fallow period

answers.name: Horticulture
answers.description: Horticulture, i.e., semi-intensive agriculture limited mainly to vegetable gardens or groves of fruit trees rather than the cultivation of field crops

answers.name: Intensive
answers.description: Intensive agriculture on permanent fields, utilizing fertilization by compost or animal manure, crop rotation, or other techniques so that fallowing is either unnecessary or is confined to relatively short periods

answers.name: Intensive irrigated
answers.description: Intensive cultivation where it is largely dependent upon irrigation

answers.name: Missing data
answers.description: Missing data

answers.name: No agriculture
answers.description: No agriculture

answers.name: Non-food
answers.description: Non-food crops only, e.g., cotton or tobacco

answers.name: Vegetables
answers.description: Vegetables, e.g., cucurbits, greens, or legumes, when more important than other crops

answers.name: Tree-fruits
answers.description: Tree fruits, e.g., bananas, breadfruit, coconuts, or dates, when more important than cereal grains and root crops. Sago, unless specifically reported to be cultivated, is treated as a gathered product rather than a cultivated one

answers.name: Roots/tubers
answers.description: Roots or tubers, e.g., manioc, potatoes, taro, or yams, when more important than cereal grains and at least as important as tree crops or vegetables

answers.name: Cereals
answers.description: Cereal grains, e.g., maize, millet, rice, or wheat, when at least as important as any other type of crop

answers.name: Missing data
answers.description: Missing data

name: Jurisdictional hierarchy beyond local community
description: The number of jurisdictional levels beyond the local community, with 1 representing the theoretical minimum (e.g.,  none/autonomous bands or villages) and 4 representing the theoretical maximum (e.g., villages nested within parishes, districts, provinces, and a complex state). This variable also provides a measure of political complexity, ranging from 1 for stateless societies, through 2 or 3 for petty and larger paramount chiefdoms or their equivalent, to 4 or 5 for large states. Note that different types of organization on the same level are counted as one, and organizations not held to be legitimate, e.g., imposed colonial regimes, are excluded.

answers.name: Acephalous
answers.description: No political authority beyond community (e.g., autonomous bands and villages)

answers.name: One level
answers.description: One level (e.g., petty chiefdoms)

answers.name: Two levels
answers.description: Two levels (e.g., larger chiefdoms)

answers.name: Three levels
answers.description: Three levels (e.g., states)

answers.name: Four levels
answers.description: Four levels (e.g., large states)

answers.name: Missing data
answers.description: Missing data

name: Class differentiation: primary
description: The degree and type of class differentiation, excluding purely political and religious statuses. See also "Class differentiation: secondary," as some societies exhibit important features of two different types of class differentation.

answers.name: Absence of distinctions
answers.description: Absence of significant class distinctions among freemen (slavery is treated in EA070), ignoring variations in individual repute achieved through skill, valor, piety, or wisdom

answers.name: Wealth distinctions
answers.description: Wealth distinctions, based on the possession or distribution of property, present and socially important but not crystallized into distinct and hereditary social classes

answers.name: Elite stratification
answers.description: Elite stratification, in which an elite class derives its superior status from, and perpetuates it through, control over scarce resources, particularly land, and is thereby differentiated from a property-less proletariat or serf class

answers.name: Dual stratification
answers.description: Dual stratification into a hereditary aristocracy and a lower class of ordinary commoners or freemen, where traditionally ascribed noble status is at least as decisive as control over scarce resources

answers.name: Complex stratification
answers.description: Complex stratification into social classes correlated in large measure with extensive differentiation of occupational statuses

answers.name: Missing data
answers.description: Missing data

name: Slavery: type
description: The forms and prevalence of slave status, treated quite independently of both class and caste status.

answers.name: Absence of slavery
answers.description: Absence or near absence of slavery

answers.name: Slavery, nonhereditary
answers.description: Incipient or nonhereditary slavery, i.e., where slave status is temporary and not transmitted to the children of slaves

answers.name: Slavery, no info on heritability
answers.description: Slavery reported but not identified as hereditary or nonhereditary

answers.name: Slavery, hereditary
answers.description: Hereditary slavery present and of at least modest social significance

answers.name: Missing data
answers.description: Missing data

name: Settlement patterns
description: The prevailing type of settlement pattern.

answers.name: Nomadic
answers.description: Fully migratory or nomadic bands

answers.name: Seminomadic
answers.description: Seminomadic communities whose members wander in bands for at least half of the year but occupy a fixed settlement at some season or seasons, e.g., recurrently occupied winter quarters

answers.name: Semisedentary
answers.description: Semisedentary communities whose members shift from one to another fixed settlement at different seasons or who occupy more or less permanently a single settlement from which a substantial proportion of the population departs seasonally to occupy shifting camps, e.g., during transhumance

answers.name: Impermanent
answers.description: Compact but impermanent settlements, i.e., villages whose location is shifted every few years

answers.name: Dispersed homesteads
answers.description: Neighborhoods of dispersed family homesteads

answers.name: Hamlets
answers.description: Separated hamlets where several such form a more or less permanent single community

answers.name: Villages/towns
answers.description: Compact and relatively permanent settlements, i.e., nucleated villages or towns

answers.name: Complex permanent
answers.description: Complex settlements consisting of a nucleated village or town with outlying homesteads or satellite hamlets. Urban aggregations of population are not separately indicated since EA031 deals with community size

answers.name: Missing data
answers.description: Missing data

description: The average population of local communities, whatever the pattern of settlement, computed from census data or other evidence.

From 50 to 99 persons
From 100 to 199 persons
From 200 to 399 persons

More than 1,000 persons in the absence of indigenous urban aggregations of more than 5,000
One or more indigenous towns of more than 5,000 inhabitants but none of more than 50,000
One or more indigenous cities with more than 50,000 inhabitants

answers.description: Missing data

name: Religion: high gods
description: The range of beliefs in high gods. A high god is defined, following Swanson, as a spiritual being who is believed to have created all reality and/or to be its ultimate governor, even if his sole act was to create other spirits who, in turn, created or control the natural world.

answers.name: Absent
answers.description: A high god absent or not reported in substantial descriptions of religious beliefs

answers.name: Otiose
answers.description: A high god present but otiose or not concerned with human affairs

answers.name: Active, but not supporting morality
answers.description: A high god present and active in human affairs but not offering positive support to human morality

answers.name: Active, supporting morality
answers.description: A high god present, active, and specifically supportive of human morality

answers.name: Missing data
answers.description: Missing data
